counterexample: Let M3 be the five-element diamond lattice {0,a,b,c,1}, ordered by 0<a,b,c<1, with a,b,c pairwise incomparable. Since M3 is finite and has all finite joins and meets (including 0 and 1), it is a complete lattice, hence an object of CLat. But it is not a frame: b∨c=1, so a∧(b∨c)=a∧1=a, whereas (a∧b)∨(a∧c)=0∨0=0. Thus finite meets do not distribute over arbitrary joins. Therefore M3 is not an object of Frm.
assessment_summary: Step 0002 incorrectly claims that every object of CLat is an object of Frm. The explicit complete lattice M3 is not a frame, so the required object inclusion fails and the proof may be stopped at this first definitive error.
